claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys occupy a broad, largely unexplored, multi-principal-element compositional space.
Combining machine learning, high-throughput CALPHAD, and DFT screening can rationally design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEAs.
The integrated computational approach can efficiently navigate the multidimensional RHEA compositional space.
Bayesian optimization can be combined with high-throughput CALPHAD simulations and DFT calculations for RHEA composition design.
The computational search can impose multiple objectives involving phase stability, strength, ductility, density, and operational temperature.
CALPHAD and DFT models can predict phase distributions and microstructural features.
Integrating the computational methods reduces the composition search space by accurately predicting phase stability.
Machine learning can refine trade-offs among strength, ductility, and weight.
Refining those property trade-offs can identify optimal RHEA compositions.
The approach will identify a focused composition regime satisfying strong, ductile, and low-weight requirements.
The integrated approach will perform better than conventional trial-and-error design at focusing the composition search.
Traditional exploratory alloy-design methods rely on sequential experimental testing without computational prescreening.
The effectiveness of the approach is limited by the accuracy of CALPHAD and DFT models.
The effectiveness of the approach is limited by the quality and scope of machine-learning training data.
The computational approach may fail to capture unexpected phase transformations under real-world conditions.
Simulated property predictions may not translate directly to experimentally measured outcomes.
Predicted properties may be sensitive to computational model parameters.
